prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1254; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a parking lot collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck while stationary. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is represented by counsel, so all contact will be routed through the attorney's office from this point forward.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the first notice of loss. They confirm several details of the scene and the position of the vehicles, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision itself. The damage to the vehicle appears consistent with the impact described.

Entry 3: Obtained the policy record, which names the driver involved as a listed driver. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and there is nothing in the file to suggest the damage predates the start of the policy period. No prior damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant's representative. The claimant's account of the event has remained the same in every conversation so far. The police report and statements from others on scene place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact.

Entry 5: Medical records reviewed. The reported injuries fit the type and force of the collision well, and no earlier injury to the same area of the body is known. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Based on the medical and physical evidence, the claim appears consistent with the reported loss. File will move to evaluation of the bodily injury component, with the attorney's office copied on the next status update.
